title: Nourishing Ethiopian Rice Pilaf
description: A fragrant, floral rice pilaf infused with berbere and ginger, finished with a touch of fermented miso for depth. It is a one‑pot dish that is crumbly, wholesome and FODMAP‑friendly.

ingredients.name: garlic‑infused oil
ingredients.notes: oil infused with garlic flavor but no pieces, FODMAP-friendly

instructions: Warm the garlic‑infused oil in a large pot over medium heat until fragrant.
Add the grated ginger, berbere spice, turmeric, and stir for 1 minute.
Toss in the carrots, cauliflower, and tomatoes, cooking until slightly softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice and coat it evenly with the spice mixture, cooking for another 2 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover the pot.
Simmer the rice for 12 minutes, partially covered, until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Gently stir in the spinach and miso paste, then cover again and cook for an additional 3 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Remove the pot from heat, squeeze fresh lemon juice over the pilaf, and fluff with a fork.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to settle.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with chopped fresh cilantro if tolerated.
